key_insight: A two-level machine-learning workflow can efficiently map phase stability across complex hybrid perovskite alloy compositions, revealing that stable regions are narrower in Sn-based alloys than in Pb-based ones.
engineering_relevance: The stability map helps screen composition choices for more durable perovskite solar absorbers, especially by identifying the high-iodide regions where stability is maximized.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials were trained on density functional theory data for fast structure relaxation.
Secondary ML models predicted energies directly from unrelaxed alloy structures.
The approach computed free-energy landscapes across composition and phase space while accounting for alloy disorder and FA molecular orientations.
evidence_signal: The models were used to evaluate free-energy landscapes for (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3, and the resulting stability trends showed no stabilization near the center of composition space.
watch_item: Because the workflow relies on ML surrogates trained on DFT data, its predictions may be sensitive to the coverage and transferability of the training set across compositions and phases.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
